title: The Dollar & Currencies
headline_read: Currency markets are calm — the dollar is near where it was a year ago.

indicators.title: Broad Dollar Index · year-over-year
indicators.context: How fast the trade-weighted dollar is rising or falling versus a year ago. Big moves in either direction are destabilizing: a surging dollar squeezes the world's dollar borrowers and crushes emerging markets; a sliding one imports inflation.
indicators.read: The dollar is down 1.8% against major currencies over the past year — a normal drift.

indicators.title: Euro · dollars per euro
indicators.context: How many dollars one euro buys. The world's second currency — a rising number means a stronger euro (and a weaker dollar) — and the cleanest mirror on dollar strength.
indicators.read: The euro is little changed against the dollar over the past year.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A market price has no inherent good-or-bad level — higher or lower isn't itself better or worse.

indicators.title: Japanese Yen · yen per dollar
indicators.context: How many yen one dollar buys — a rising number means a WEAKER yen. Japan's currency anchors Asia's funding markets; a violent yen move tends to ripple through global markets.
indicators.read: The yen has weakened 7.1% against the dollar over the past year.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A market price has no inherent good-or-bad level — higher or lower isn't itself better or worse.

indicators.title: Chinese Yuan · yuan per dollar
indicators.context: How many yuan one dollar buys — a rising number means a WEAKER yuan. Beijing manages this rate; a deliberate slide makes Chinese exports cheaper and tends to escalate trade tensions.
indicators.read: The yuan has strengthened 6.4% against the dollar over the past year.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A market price has no inherent good-or-bad level — higher or lower isn't itself better or worse.
